title: A scene of things doing something together is drawn as one scene: a cat playing a piano
goal: When a person asks for several things in a relationship ('a cartoon cat playing a piano', 'a dog chasing a ball', 'a fox sleeping under a tree'), Ask draws one picture where they really do that: the cat sits at the piano, its paws on the keys, both at sensible sizes and in one style. Today it drops two stock drawings on top of each other.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20 15:35 (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-playing-piano.png): asked 'draw a piano with a cartoon cat playing it'. Ask made two add_drawing steps (row 'Drew 2 drawings'): a built-in cat drawing (Twemoji-style, the dog task's built-in set) placed over most of a built-in upright piano, which shows only as a dark edge behind the cat. User: 'It stuffed a cat on top of some keys. horrible. but it makes some logical sense.'

Cause, likely: the planner splits a scene into nouns and calls add_drawing per noun (Sources/PhotonzCore/AskPlanning.swift, instructions around :504 say add_drawing once with its subject); nothing plans the relationship, pose or placement. Waits on the illustration task (in progress), whose passes (composition, shapes, light) are where a scene belongs.
acceptance: 'draw a piano with a cartoon cat playing it' on a blank picture gives a cat seated or standing at the piano, facing the keys, paws on the keys, the piano in a view where the keys show, the two at believable relative sizes, nothing of one hidden by the other by accident, in one shared style and palette

The relationship is planned before drawing (who, where, doing what, which parts touch, what is in front), and the plan is checked from the read document: the paws' layers touch the keys' layer, the cat overlaps the piano only where the plan says

The built-in drawings are used only when they can be posed for the scene (for example a cat that can sit and reach); otherwise the scene is drawn as one illustration in the artist's passes of an-illustration-ask-draws-looks-illustrated-natu

Six scene cases join the eval (a cat playing a piano, a dog chasing a ball, a fox sleeping under a tree, a robot watering a plant, a bird on a branch singing, a child flying a kite), each scoring 7 or more on didWhatWasAsked and designed; the user's picture (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-cat-playing-piano.png) scores 3 or lower on didWhatWasAsked

The row names the scene ('Drew a cat playing a piano'), and the whole scene is one change. Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after contact sheets and scores. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not
